category: hosted tcp and http tunnel (developer service)

free_tier.stated: Free with an account; the Dev tunnels limits table sets 5 GB of bandwidth per user, reset monthly.

egress.terms: 5 GB per user per month, stated in the Dev tunnels limits table; the same table caps a tunnel at 20 MB/s, 10 tunnels per user and 1500 HTTP requests per minute per port.; ingress: tcp
egress.free_allowance: 5 GB per user per month, stated in the Dev tunnels limits table; the same table caps a tunnel at 20 MB/s, 10 tunnels per user and 1500 HTTP requests per minute per port.

tooling: devtunnel CLI, VS Code and Visual Studio integration.
chaining: Free TCP ingress for a free VM, with no card and no published cap.

limits.value: 5 GB of bandwidth per user, reset monthly
1500 HTTP requests per minute per port
data transfer rate up to 20 MB/s per tunnel

binding_note: 5 GB is 0.0045 TiB, so the byte allowance fails about 220 times before 1 TiB/month. Ports are TCP, with UDP hedged as 'may also be supported', so a WireGuard peer has no reliable path.

identity_cost.detail: 'All creation of dev tunnels requires either a Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft, or GitHub account.'

reliability_note: Designed for development traffic; the aggregator records that visitors see warnings on the URLs.
confidence_note: The allowance, the rate and the tunnel count are stated in one table. What is not stated is whether the 5 GB covers raw TCP forwarding as well as HTTP; the table names no protocol.

evidence.proved: 'Tunnel port - An IP port number (1-65535) that is allowed through a dev tunnel'; 'most often linked to TCP connections on either side, but UDP-based protocols may also be supported'
creating a tunnel requires an Entra ID, Microsoft or GitHub account; anonymous users cannot create tunnels
'## Dev tunnels limits'; 'Bandwidth | 5 GB per user'; 'Tunnels | 10 per user'; 'Data transfer rate | Up to 20 MB/s per tunnel'; 'The limits reset monthly'

notes: Corrected in the sweep's last pass: the overview and the FAQ state no quota, and the limits table does. 5 GB/month makes this a development endpoint, not an ingress path. The 20 MB/s ceiling is per tunnel and would allow 1 TiB in about 15 hours, so the monthly byte quota is what binds.
